findings.title: Time as joined intervals

findings.mechanism: The focus noun carries an interval of time; the two occurrences of tawaṣaw in 103:3 provide an independent joining relation. Their contact makes the span feel connected and transmitted through successive acts, rather than an empty container.
findings.reader_payoff: Time becomes perceptible as something lived through connected practices and shared across intervals.
findings.containment: The joining is a pericope-level image, not a claim that al-ʿaṣr lexically means joining or that the repeated counsel proves a chronology. The ordinary temporal oath remains intact; a live alternative is that the repetition only links two duties.

epistemic.reason: The surface and pericope context are supplied; the relation is a bounded contextual synthesis rather than a lexical replacement.

findings.title: Pressure held for a possible yield
findings.claim: The focus's press meets the exception's reciprocal counsel, restraint, and attributed stopper image, turning pressure into a vessel that can be held long enough to yield instead of rupture.
findings.mechanism: Al-ʿaṣr supplies sustained pressing; tawaṣaw supplies shared maintenance; al-ṣabr supplies restraint and, in the attributed trace, a stopper that keeps contents from escaping. Their contact changes pressure from an uncontained force into a maintained vessel.
findings.reader_payoff: The closing patience and mutual counsel appear as practices that contain pressure and preserve the possibility of yield.
findings.containment: The stopper branch is unresolved and remains attributed; the vessel is an analogy, not a lexical gloss of al-ʿaṣr or al-ṣabr. A live alternative is that the stopper image is too distant and patience is simply moral endurance.

epistemic.reason: Exact surface anchors are supplied, but the HFT trace is legacy_unbound; its semantic links remain attributed and qualified.

findings.title: The temporal span under a day of recompense
findings.claim: The temporal oath in 103:1 gains a specific horizon when placed beside 1:4's day of recompense: the span's exposure and loss now open toward an appointed reckoning.
findings.mechanism: Al-ʿaṣr carries time as a span; the individually supplied external ayah 1:4 names a day of recompense. Their temporal contact gives the span an endpoint of accounting beyond the immediate pericope's statement of loss.
findings.reader_payoff: The reader can perceive a horizon of reckoning behind the oath's time without making the time-word itself name that day.
findings.containment: This is an external overlay from 1:4 alone. It does not claim that al-ʿaṣr means the Day of Recompense, that 1:4 is an implicit whole-surah frame, or that the two passages are lexically identical.

epistemic.reason: The surface and pericope context are supplied; the relation is a bounded contextual synthesis rather than a lexical replacement.
